    # AWS Documentation MCP Server

    This server provides tools to access public AWS documentation, search for content, and get recommendations.

    ## Best Practices

    - For long documentation pages, make multiple calls to `read_documentation` with different `start_index` values for pagination
    - By default, use read_sections when the answer could be within a specific section(s), given the table of contents. Otherwise, use read_documentation to scan the entire page.
    - For very long documents (>30,000 characters), stop reading if you've found the needed information
    - When searching, use specific technical terms rather than general phrases
    - Use `recommend` tool to discover related content that might not appear in search results
    - For recent updates to a service, get an URL for any page in that service, then check the **New** section of the `recommend` tool output on that URL
    - If multiple searches with similar terms yield insufficient results, pivot to using `recommend` to find related pages.
    - Always cite the documentation URL when providing information to users

    ## Tool Selection Guide

    - Use `search_documentation` when: You need to find documentation about a specific AWS service or feature
    - Use `read_documentation` when: You have a specific documentation URL and need its content
    - Use `read_sections` when: You have a specific documentation URL and specific section title(s) and want content from those specific section(s)
    - Use `recommend` when: You want to find related content to a documentation page you're already viewing or need to find newly released information
    - Use `recommend` as a fallback when: Multiple searches have not yielded the specific information needed

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. name: TI-1446 PG Metrics Pipeline — WIP pausado 2026-04-23
description: postgres_exporter 0.17.1 deployado en lms-db VM con custom queries funcionando. Falta wire Ops Agent scrape → Cloud Monitoring + 4 rules DB en Grafana. Pipeline local validado, métricas no llegan a Cloud Monitoring todavía.
type: project
originSessionId: 47a1c06c-c6d3-410e-bc1f-f7feca7e7d35
---
## Estado al pausar (pos-deploy 21:00 UTC)

**Pipeline local ✅** — postgres_exporter expone 5 metric families en `http://127.0.0.1:9187/metrics` en la VM `lms-db`. Validado con `curl` local.

**Pipeline cloud ⏳** — Ops Agent config todavía vanilla (sin prometheus receiver). Las métricas NO están llegando a Cloud Monitoring aún.

**Grafana rules DB ⏳** — las 4 rules (idle-in-tx, saturation, repl lag, blocking) no escritas porque dependen del pipeline cloud.

## Lo que está live ahora en `lms-db` VM

```
/usr/local/bin/postgres_exporter         # binary v0.17.1
/etc/postgres_exporter/queries.yaml      # 5 custom queries, mode 0640 root:postgres_exporter
/etc/postgres_exporter/postgres_exporter.env   # DSN con claude_readonly creds
/etc/systemd/system/postgres_exporter.service  # systemd unit, enabled + active
```

Linux user `postgres_exporter` creado (system, nologin).
Puerto 9187 solo en loopback (no expuesto a red).

## DSN usado

Reutilizamos `claude_readonly` (el user del mcp-postgres de openfang). Ya es miembro de `pg_monitor` (role built-in PG 10+) → tiene acceso a pg_stat_* completo.

Password obtenida de `POSTGRES_CONNECTION_URL` en `/opt/openfang/.env` del VM openfang (no duplicamos secret).

**No se creó nuevo user en DB** (decisión explícita del usuario: "usa el usuario y password que tienes para el mcp de postgres, no crees ningún usuario de db").

## Métricas expuestas (validadas en prod live)

Observación 21:00 UTC:

| Métrica | Valor observado | Semántica |
|---|---|---|
| `pg_connection_saturation_saturation_ratio` | 0.6894 | 586/850 max_connections — healthy (<0.80) |
| `pg_connection_saturation_current_connections` | 586 | |
| `pg_connection_saturation_max_connections` | 850 | |
| `pg_idle_in_tx_by_app_count{app="unknown"}` | 4 | normal |
| `pg_blocking_queries_blocked_over_{60,120,300}s` | 0 | sin bloqueos sostenidos ahora |
| `pg_replication_status_reply_lag_seconds` | 0.04s (replica 10.212.6.30), 0.06s (10.212.6.31) | 2 replicas streaming healthy |
| `pg_stat_activity_by_app_count` | ~50 series por (state, app, datname) | distribución completa |

## Próximos pasos cuando retomemos

### 1. Ops Agent scrape (5 min, low risk)

Editar `/etc/google-cloud-ops-agent/config.yaml` (vanilla actualmente) agregando:

```yaml
metrics:
  receivers:
    prometheus_pg_exporter:
      type: prometheus
      config:
        scrape_configs:
          - job_name: postgres_exporter
            scrape_interval: 60s
            static_configs:
              - targets: ["127.0.0.1:9187"]
  service:
    pipelines:
      postgres:
        receivers: [prometheus_pg_exporter]
```

Luego `sudo systemctl restart google-cloud-ops-agent`.

### 2. Validar llegada a Cloud Monitoring (5 min)

Consultar en Grafana datasource `cloud-monitoring-main` el metric `prometheus.googleapis.com/pg_connection_saturation_saturation_ratio/gauge`. Debe aparecer con los labels `instance_id, zone` (gce_instance) + los de la metric.

### 3. 4 alert rules DB (10 min)

En `sec/grafana-config/alert-rules.tf` agregar al `grafana_rule_group.infra_critical`:

- **Rule 10: PG idle-in-tx leak** (P0, for 5m): `max by (application_name) (pg_idle_in_tx_by_app_count) > 10`
- **Rule 11: PG connections saturation** (P1, for 5m): `pg_connection_saturation_saturation_ratio > 0.80`
- **Rule 12: PG replication lag** (P1, for 5m): `max(pg_replication_status_replay_lag_seconds) > 30`
- **Rule 13: PG blocking query >2min** (P0, for 2m): `pg_blocking_queries_blocked_over_120s > 0`

Todas con datasource `cloud-monitoring-main` + `no_data_state=OK`.

### 4. Commit (5 min)

Crear directorio `databases/vm/files/monitoring/` en el repo con:
- `queries.yaml` (copia de /etc/postgres_exporter/queries.yaml)
- `postgres_exporter.service` (systemd unit)
- `README.md` con setup + smoke test reproducible
- `ops-agent-receiver.yaml` snippet (para referencia)

### 5. Linear TI-1446 (2 min)

Update con progress comment + si todo OK, close.

## Gotchas encontrados durante el deploy

1. **Flag syntax cambió en v0.17.1**: `--auto-discover-databases=false` no funciona; es `--no-auto-discover-databases`. Fix aplicado.
2. **queries.yaml format DEPRECATED warning**: el formato extended queries está en camino de deprecation pero funcional. Upstream mueve a "collectors" system. No blocker para nosotros.
3. **Replica_name label colision**: `application_name` de `pg_stat_replication` es siempre "walreceiver" → duplicate label entre replicas. Fix: usar `host(client_addr)::text` como label único (10.212.6.30 y 10.212.6.31).

## Estado sessions activas

- TI-1445 Fase 1 **DONE** (9 rules grafana + sidecar + firewall).
- TI-1446 **en progreso** (este file).
- TI-1443 Slack dedup (DMs) pendiente acción manual.
- TI-1444 tokens optim pendiente.
- Findings DB (transaction leak orders-domain + advisory locks services-domain) correlacionan con worker timeouts gunicorn — escalar al team apps como follow-up.

## Cómo retomar

1. SSH: `ssh lmsprod` (alias configurado).
2. Verificar exporter: `sudo systemctl status postgres_exporter` → active (running).
3. Verificar metrics: `curl -s localhost:9187/metrics | grep -c '^pg_'` → 53056+ lines.
4. Seguir con pasos 1-5 arriba.

content.content:
# sec/grafana-config — Grafana Dashboard Provisioning

## What This Module Does
Provisions Grafana dashboards and folders as code via Terraform. Currently manages KPI dashboards from the observability platform (DevLake). Will be extended in v1.1 to include Google Cloud Monitoring infrastructure dashboards.

## State
- **Backend**: GCS bucket `liftit-tf-state`, prefix `sec/grafana-config`
- **Workspaces**: Single workspace (Grafana is centralized on the observability VM)

## Resources Created
- `grafana_folder.kpi` — KPI Dashboards folder (uid: `kpi-dashboards`)
- `grafana_dashboard.kpi_overview` — Main KPI dashboard with 4 stat panels (deployment success rate, system uptime, scope completion, deploy duration)

## Configuration
- **Grafana URL**: `https://observability.liftit.co`
- **Datasource UID**: `P430005175C4C7810` (DevLake MySQL datasource)
- **Dashboard JSON**: `dashboard.json` rendered via `templatefile()` with datasource UID injection
- **Secrets**: SOPS encrypted (`secrets/grafana-api-key.enc.yaml`)

## Dependencies
- Grafana instance running on observability VM (`sec/observability`)
- Grafana API key for Terraform provider auth (SOPS encrypted)

## Providers
- Terraform `~> 1.14`, Grafana `~> 3.0`, SOPS `~> 1.1`

## v1.1 Planned Additions
This module will be extended (or a sibling `sec/grafana-monitoring` created) to add:
- `grafana_data_source` — Google Cloud Monitoring datasource (type `stackdriver`, JWT auth)
- `grafana_folder` — Infrastructure monitoring folder
- `grafana_dashboard` — Per-service dashboards (Cloud Run, GKE, Compute Engine, Load Balancer, shared infra)
- Dashboard auto-generation from Terraform app definitions in `apps/`, `databases/`, `common/`, `bi/`, `sec/`
- Template variables for project/environment selector across all dashboards

# Ops Agent prometheus receiver snippet for lms-db (TI-1446).
# Append to /etc/google-cloud-ops-agent/config.yaml, then:
#   sudo systemctl restart google-cloud-ops-agent
# Validar que pg_* metrics llegan a Cloud Monitoring:
#   metric.type="prometheus.googleapis.com/pg_connection_saturation_saturation_ratio/gauge"
# Resource type destino: prometheus_target
#   (labels: cluster=__gce__, instance=127.0.0.1:9187, job=postgres_exporter,
#    namespace=<instance_id>/<instance_name>, project_id, location=<zone>).

metrics:
  receivers:
    prometheus_pg_exporter:
      type: prometheus
      config:
        scrape_configs:
          - job_name: postgres_exporter
            scrape_interval: 60s
            static_configs:
              - targets: ["127.0.0.1:9187"]
  service:
    pipelines:
      postgres:
        receivers: [prometheus_pg_exporter]

# Liftit PG Metrics Pipeline (TI-1446)

Lightweight PostgreSQL metrics collection for proactive alerting. Runs on
the `lms-db` VM (primary). No database user creation needed: reuses
`claude_readonly` which already holds `pg_monitor` role (superset of
`pg_stat_*` views).

## Pipeline
```
postgres_exporter v0.17.1 (loopback :9187)
    └── scraped by Google Cloud Ops Agent (prometheus receiver, 60s)
        └── exported as prometheus_target in Cloud Monitoring
            └── queried by Grafana cloud-monitoring-main datasource
                └── alert rules (sec/grafana-config/alert-rules.tf, rules 10-13)
```

## Files
- `queries.yaml` — custom SQL queries (5 metric families: idle-in-tx,
  saturation, blocking, replication, activity-by-app).
- `postgres_exporter.service` — systemd unit (hardened: ProtectSystem,
  NoNewPrivileges, private tmp, etc.).
- `ops-agent-receiver.yaml` — scrape config appended to Ops Agent
  `/etc/google-cloud-ops-agent/config.yaml`.

## Deploy (manual — not yet Terraformed)
```bash
# 1. Binary (from GitHub releases)
curl -LO https://github.com/prometheus-community/postgres_exporter/releases/download/v0.17.1/postgres_exporter-0.17.1.linux-amd64.tar.gz
tar -xzf postgres_exporter-0.17.1.linux-amd64.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 -o root -g root postgres_exporter-0.17.1.linux-amd64/postgres_exporter /usr/local/bin/

# 2. System user
sudo useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin postgres_exporter

# 3. Config dir + files
sudo mkdir -p /etc/postgres_exporter
sudo install -m 0640 -o root -g postgres_exporter queries.yaml /etc/postgres_exporter/queries.yaml
sudo tee /etc/postgres_exporter/postgres_exporter.env > /dev/null <<EOF
DATA_SOURCE_NAME='postgresql://claude_readonly:<PASSWORD>@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable'
EOF
sudo chmod 0640 /etc/postgres_exporter/postgres_exporter.env
sudo chown root:postgres_exporter /etc/postgres_exporter/postgres_exporter.env

# 4. Systemd unit
sudo install -m 0644 postgres_exporter.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now postgres_exporter

# 5. Ops Agent scrape — append ops-agent-receiver.yaml to config
sudo tee -a /etc/google-cloud-ops-agent/config.yaml < ops-agent-receiver.yaml
sudo systemctl restart google-cloud-ops-agent
```

## Smoke test
```bash
# Local (on the VM):
curl -s localhost:9187/metrics | grep -c '^pg_'     # expect >50k lines
curl -s localhost:9187/metrics | grep pg_connection_saturation_saturation_ratio

# Cloud Monitoring (after ~2min):
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://monitoring.googleapis.com/v3/projects/prod-apps-454414/timeSeries?filter=metric.type%3D%22prometheus.googleapis.com%2Fpg_connection_saturation_saturation_ratio%2Fgauge%22&interval.startTime=$(date -u -d '-5 min' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)&interval.endTime=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
```

## Password
Obtenida desde `/opt/openfang/.env` (var `POSTGRES_CONNECTION_URL`) en la
VM `openfang`. Rota con openfang's DSN — cuando se rote, actualizar también
`/etc/postgres_exporter/postgres_exporter.env` en `lms-db` y reiniciar.

## Gotchas encontrados durante el deploy inicial (2026-04-23)
1. Flag rename en v0.17.1: `--auto-discover-databases=false` no funciona;
   el flag correcto es `--no-auto-discover-databases`.
2. `queries.yaml` extended format tiene deprecation warning. Sigue
   funcional. Upstream está migrando a un "collectors" system — cuando
   suba a v0.20+ hay que migrar.
3. Label collision en `pg_stat_replication`: `application_name` es siempre
   "walreceiver" para todas las replicas. Workaround: usar
   `host(client_addr)::text` como label único (ver `queries.yaml`).

## Alert rules mapeadas
| Rule | Metric | Threshold | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 PG idle-in-tx leak | `pg_idle_in_tx_by_app_count` | >10 for 5m | P0 |
| 11 PG connections saturation | `pg_connection_saturation_saturation_ratio` | >0.80 for 5m | P1 |
| 12 PG replication replay lag | `pg_replication_status_replay_lag_seconds` | >30s for 5m | P1 |
| 13 PG blocking queries >2min | `pg_blocking_queries_blocked_over_120s` | >0 for 2m | P0 |

Rules vivas en `sec/grafana-config/alert-rules.tf:grafana_rule_group.infra_critical`.

input.body:
✅ Pipeline completo + 4 alert rules DB live en Grafana (commit 8a5d5e6).

## Deploy
- `postgres_exporter v0.17.1` en lms-db VM (loopback :9187, systemd enabled)
- Reusa `claude_readonly` (ya es `pg_monitor`) — no se creó user nuevo
- 5 métric families: connection saturation, idle-in-tx, blocking, replication, activity
- Ops Agent `prometheus_pg_exporter` receiver configurado, scrape 60s
- Validado E2E: metric llega a Cloud Monitoring como `prometheus.googleapis.com/pg_connection_saturation_saturation_ratio/gauge` (value: 0.6965 healthy)

## 4 Alert rules creadas (rules 10-13)
| Rule | Metric | Threshold | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 PG idle-in-tx leak | `pg_idle_in_tx_by_app_count` by application_name | >10 for 5m | P0 |
| 11 PG connections saturation | `pg_connection_saturation_saturation_ratio` | >0.80 for 5m | P1 |
| 12 PG replication replay lag | `pg_replication_status_replay_lag_seconds` by replica_addr | >30s for 5m | P1 |
| 13 PG blocking queries >2min | `pg_blocking_queries_blocked_over_120s` | >0 for 2m | P0 |

Todas con `no_data_state=OK` + `exec_err_state=OK` + unpaused. Datasource `cloud-monitoring-main`, projectName `prod-apps-454414`.

## Files commited (8a5d5e6)
- `sec/grafana-config/alert-rules.tf` +299 líneas (rules 10-13)
- `databases/vm/files/monitoring/queries.yaml` (5 custom SQL)
- `databases/vm/files/monitoring/postgres_exporter.service` (systemd unit hardened)
- `databases/vm/files/monitoring/ops-agent-receiver.yaml` (scrape snippet)
- `databases/vm/files/monitoring/README.md` (deploy + smoke test + gotchas)

## Gotchas encontrados
1. Flag rename v0.17.1: `--auto-discover-databases=false` no funciona; usar `--no-auto-discover-databases`.
2. Extended queries.yaml format está deprecado upstream (collectors system nuevo) pero funcional.
3. `pg_stat_replication` tiene label collision (`application_name="walreceiver"` igual para ambas replicas); workaround `host(client_addr)::text`.

## Métricas baseline observadas (healthy)
- Saturation: 0.69 (586/850 max_connections)
- Idle-in-tx: 4 (app=unknown) — normal
- Blocking >60/120/300s: 0
- Replay lag: 0.04s-0.06s ambas replicas streaming

Ticket listo para cerrar.

{"id":"TI-1446","title":"PG metrics pipeline — postgres_exporter + Ops Agent scrape para alertas DB proactivas","description":"## Contexto

<issue id="a318116e-300b-4419-b2f8-b58f744f3c23">TI-1445</issue> Fase 1 deployó 3 rules de infra (CrashLoop, 5xx linkerd, disk). La segunda wave prioriza **DB** — vimos hoy en prod dos incidentes reales no alertados: transaction leak en `app_orders_domain` (9+ conns idle-in-tx 2-7 min) y advisory lock contention en `app_services_domain` correlacionado con WORKER TIMEOUT de gunicorn.

PG de Liftit corre en GCE VM (`databases/vm` module), no Cloud SQL. El pipeline de métricas hoy es:

* Google Ops Agent instalado → envía cpu/disk/memory a Cloud Monitoring
* *NO hay postgres_exporter, NO hay pg_stat\_* en pipeline observable\*

## Objetivo

Exponer las métricas pg_stat\_\* necesarias para 4 rules de alertas DB **sin saturar la VM de PG**. Elegimos Opción B (evaluamos 3):

* **B: postgres_exporter sidecar → Ops Agent Prometheus scrape → Cloud Monitoring** ← esta

Detalles evaluación de opciones en `.planning/phases/07-.../SESSION-2026-04-23.md`.

## Arquitectura

```
PG VM (databases/vm prod)
  ├── postgres (existente)
  ├── postgres_exporter (NUEVO, systemd service, binario upstream)
  │     └── listen localhost:9187 (no externo)
  └── google-cloud-ops-agent (existente)
        └── nuevo pipeline prometheus scrape localhost:9187
              └── envía a Cloud Monitoring → prometheus.googleapis.com/*
                    └── queryable via datasource `cloud-monitoring-main` en Grafana
```

Load en PG estimado: **\~35 queries × 1/min = 2100/hora**. Traffic actual \~cientos qps business. Delta = 0.01%. Invisible.

## DoD

### Provisioning

- [ ] Crear user `monitoring_readonly` en PG con rol built-in `pg_monitor` (PG 10+).

  ```sql
  CREATE USER monitoring_readonly WITH PASSWORD '<generated>';
  GRANT pg_monitor TO monitoring_readonly;
  ```
- [ ] Password en SOPS: `databases/vm/secrets/secrets.enc.yaml` key `monitoring_readonly_password`.

### postgres_exporter deployment

- [ ] Descargar binario `postgres_exporter` v0.15+ desde [github.com/prometheus-community/postgres_exporter](<http://github.com/prometheus-community/postgres_exporter>).
- [ ] Systemd unit `/etc/systemd/system/postgres_exporter.service` corriendo como user dedicado (uid fuera de postgres), `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/postgres_exporter --web.listen-address=127.0.0.1:9187 --auto-discover-databases=false --collector.custom_queries --extend.query-path=/etc/postgres_exporter/custom-queries.yaml`.
- [ ] `DATA_SOURCE_NAME=postgresql://monitoring_readonly:$PWD@localhost:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable` (loopback, no necesita SSL).
- [ ] `/etc/postgres_exporter/custom-queries.yaml` con queries para:
  * `pg_stat_activity_by_state_app` — count(\*) by state, application_name, datname
  * `pg_replication_lag_seconds` — extract(epoch from now()-pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp())
  * `pg_blocking_queries` — count de queries con wait_event_type='Lock' y duration>60s
  * `pg_connection_saturation` — numbackends/max_connections ratio

### Ops Agent scrape

- [ ] Editar `/etc/google-cloud-ops-agent/config.yaml` agregando pipeline prometheus scrape a `localhost:9187`, interval 60s.
- [ ] `systemctl restart google-cloud-ops-agent`.
- [ ] Validar en Cloud Monitoring: las métricas aparecen como `prometheus.googleapis.com/pg_*` queryables.

### Terraform integration (no cambios existentes, pero documentación)

- [ ] Actualizar `databases/vm/CLAUDE.md` con la sección "Monitoring".
- [ ] Commitear los scripts de deployment + custom-queries.yaml en el repo (`databases/vm/files/monitoring/`).

### Smoke test

- [ ] Desde Grafana UI (o API) query a `pg_stat_activity_by_state_app` en datasource cloud-monitoring-main → ver series con labels state/application_name.
- [ ] Forzar un `BEGIN;` en un psql session y dejarlo idle → la métrica debe subir el counter `state="idle in transaction"` dentro de 60s.

### Downstream — 4 alert rules (en sesión siguiente, gateadas por este issue)

- [ ] Rule: PG idle-in-tx leak (P0) — count{state="idle in transaction"} por application_name > 10 for 5m.
- [ ] Rule: PG connections saturation (P1) — connection_saturation > 0.80 for 5m.
- [ ] Rule: PG replication lag (P1) — replication_lag_seconds > 30 for 5m.
- [ ] Rule: PG blocking query >2min (P0) — blocking_queries_count > 0 for 2m.

## Riesgos

| Riesgo | Mitigación |
| -- | -- |
| postgres_exporter cae o crashea → métricas se pierden silenciosamente | Ops Agent loggea scrape failures; crear rule adicional `prometheus scrape target down` más adelante. |
| Custom query mal escrita genera full table scan | Todas las queries van contra pg_stat\_\* (shared memory views), nunca tablas de datos. Peer review del YAML antes de deploy. |
| User monitoring_readonly con perms insuficientes en PG <10 | Liftit corre PG 17 (confirmado en pg-health audit) — rol pg_monitor built-in existe desde PG 10. |
| Pipeline duplicado (postgres_exporter + Ops Agent PG receiver native) | No mezclar. Usar SOLO el scrape vía Ops Agent. Deshabilitar el receiver postgresql nativo si ya estuviera activo. |
| PG primary vs replica confusión | Deploy en **primary** (lectura de pg_stat_activity local). Replication lag se mide desde primary via pg_stat_replication. Para alerts de replica-side (replica caída), considerar exporter también en replica (futuro). |

## Dependencias

* Acceso SSH al VM de PG primary (vía VPN o IAP).
* Grants de superuser en PG (una vez, para crear user + asignar rol).
* Permisos para escribir en SOPS del módulo databases/vm.

{"id":"TI-1444","title":"OpenFang — optimizar tokens: bajar default limit de mcp_logging 50→20 + evaluar session compaction","description":"## Contexto

Observación 2026-04-23: loops del `assistant` consumen 130K-268K tokens cada uno. El grueso viene de tool_results de `mcp_logging_list_log_entries` que devuelven **50 entries por default** con textPayload de 200-500 chars cada uno — \~25K tokens por query, \~75K tokens si el loop encadena 3 queries a logs.

Para \~57 loops/día (ventana observada 3h): **5.4M tokens totales**, **\~$0.85 USD/día**. Proyección mensual \~$25 USD — bajo el budget de $280/mes, pero hay ganancia clara si se reduce el payload.

## Tareas

### 1\. Bajar default limit del MCP logging (quick win, \~30min)

En `apps/ai/files/mcp-logging/`:

- [ ] Revisar handler del tool `list_log_entries` — bajar default `limit` de 50 a 20.
- [ ] Subir tag de imagen a `mcp-logging:0.X.Y+1`.
- [ ] Deploy al VM: `cd /opt/openfang && sudo docker compose up -d openfang-mcp-logging`.
- [ ] Smoke test con una query de logs desde el bot.

Impacto estimado: **\~40% menos tokens** en queries de logs. Cuando el LLM necesita más de 20 entries puede pasar `limit=50` explícitamente.

### 2\. Evaluar session compaction (\~2h investigación)

Observación: el context del loop sube hasta 243K tokens en algunos casos — el historial acumulado del assistant está empujando al LLM a replayar respuestas previas. OpenFang 0.5.9 tiene `session_repair` (trim mensajes viejos) pero no exposición clara de TTL por agent.

- [ ] Investigar si openfang tiene `session_ttl_hours` o `max_messages_per_session` expuesto en config (config.toml `[agents.<name>]` o CLI).
- [ ] Si existe: aplicar al `assistant` (ej. reset diario, o max 20 turnos).
- [ ] Si no existe: evaluar un cron de `openfang` CLI que haga `session clear` o similar al inicio del día.
- [ ] Medir impacto en tokens totales.

### 3\. Opcional — prompt trimming (futuro)

El system_prompt del assistant creció a \~260 líneas / 7.9KB (\~2000 tokens input por cada loop). Es el precio del comportamiento estable ganado hoy, pero si se detecta redundancia se puede consolidar. **No ejecutar** sin eval framework (ver DoD original de <issue id="665ea827-84e5-4555-b530-d7377a7bde93">TI-1425</issue> Fase D).
